# Data access process

How data gets into the systems in this portfolio, who may see it, and how a team adopting the work should
handle real data. The portfolio itself only uses synthetic data; the steps for real data are the process I
would follow and that the code is built to support, not something that has been carried out with real
records yet.

## Rule one: synthetic data only in the repositories

* Every dataset in every repository is generated by seeded code, so the same seed gives the same data.
* Company names, people and records are fictional (for example a fictional grocer in the Fabric repository
  and a fictional freight company in the FinOps repository).
* Tests check that generated data is deterministic, and repository hygiene tests look for secrets and real
  identifiers.
* No real customer, patient or employee data may be committed, even in a branch. If it happens, the
  `SECURITY.md` process applies.

## How a team requests access to real data

The process an adopting team should run before any real data reaches an agent:

| Step | Who | What happens | Record kept |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Request | Requesting team | Names the use case, the datasets, the fields, the purpose and the retention period | Access request (issue or ticket) |
| 2. Classify | Data owner | Labels each field (public, internal, confidential, personal, special category) | Data sheet for the dataset |
| 3. Minimise | Data owner with the requester | Removes fields the use case does not need; masks or pseudonymises personal fields | Updated data sheet |
| 4. Assess risk | Risk reviewer | Adds or updates the risk card; high-risk use cases need sign-off before data moves | Risk card and sign-off in the audit log |
| 5. Grant | Platform owner | Grants least-privilege, role-based access to a managed identity, never to a shared account | Role assignment in IaC, reviewed in a pull request |
| 6. Monitor | Platform owner | Access is logged; unusual queries raise an alert | Log Analytics queries and alerts |
| 7. Review and expire | Data owner | Access is reviewed on a fixed cadence and removed when the purpose ends | Review entry in the audit log |

## How the code supports this

| Control | Where it exists today |
|---|---|
| Data sheets per dataset | [Model risk registry](https://github.com/jagadishmazure-jpg/Jagadish-agentic-ai-model-risk/blob/main/docs/pillars/data-sheets.md) |
| Field-level masking and row-level filtering for an agent | [Fabric data agent guardrails](https://github.com/jagadishmazure-jpg/Jagadish-fabric-enterprise-bi/blob/main/src/fabricbi/serve/guardrails.py) |
| Catalog, lineage and sensitivity labels | [Governance catalog](https://github.com/jagadishmazure-jpg/Jagadish-fabric-enterprise-bi/blob/main/governance/catalog.yaml), [lineage](https://github.com/jagadishmazure-jpg/Jagadish-fabric-enterprise-bi/blob/main/src/fabricbi/governance/lineage.py) |
| User-scoped access to enterprise systems (on-behalf-of) | [Identity gateway](https://github.com/jagadishmazure-jpg/Jagadish-azure-ai-integration-platform/blob/main/docs/components/identity-gateway.md) |
| Access-controlled retrieval (documents filtered by the caller's groups) | [Knowledge and context](https://github.com/jagadishmazure-jpg/Jagadish-azure-agent-platform/blob/main/docs/components/knowledge-and-context.md) |
| PII redaction before a model sees text | [Ticket triage redaction](https://github.com/jagadishmazure-jpg/Jagadish-agentic-ai/blob/main/projects/02-ticket-triage/ticket_triage/pii.py) |
| Sign-off with an audit chain | [HITL sign-off](https://github.com/jagadishmazure-jpg/Jagadish-agentic-ai-model-risk/blob/main/docs/components/hitl-signoff.md) |

## What an agent may and may not do with data

* Read only what the calling user may read; agents never hold broader access than their user.
* Use read-only tools for data questions; writes go through a separate tool that needs approval.
* Never send personal fields to a model when a masked or aggregated form answers the question.
* Never write raw prompts or responses with personal data to logs; logs keep identifiers and hashes.

## Limits

* None of these steps has been run with real data, a real data owner or a real risk reviewer.
* Self-service access (a catalog where teams request and receive access automatically) is not built.
* Retention and deletion are described here but not automated in the repositories.
